items.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025
items.q: this time I decided to ask him to be a special guest... And that’s where I was going to put him... And he said, “Well who’s your bass player?” I said, “Dean Johnson.” He said, “Can I use his bass?”

ctx.x: George — oh no, I can’t quite remember his name — was one of the Skylarks, and he was from Reading. And Ronny wrote those kinds of hip arrangements. And so there I was every Thursday and Sunday singing with real musicians, real jazz musicians. And that was the first time I heard a Dizzy Gillespie record. “Dizzy Atmosphere.” And that’s when I discovered jazz. And Ron kept on going, he was a great harmonica player as well, lived in L.A. and we kept in touch somehow, in a funny way, after years after that. But that…
formed the first jazz club because there was no jazz out there. In fact the conservatory wouldn’t let us use the conservatory piano for the concert when we brought Dave Brubeck in.
